sentences.text: Respondent  Writ Petition filed under  Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying for issuance   For Petitioner : Mr.S.Lakshmanasamy  For respondent : Mr.H.Yasmeen Ali  ORDER

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner praying for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus, to direct the respondent to draw joint samples from the consignment of the petitioner under Bill of Entry No.2967947 dated 19.10.2015 and send the same for lab testing in terms of the Notification No.1-17/FSSAI/T/2010, dated 20.01.2012, issued by the respondent within a time frame.

M.Janardhanan vs The Authorized Officer on 29 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44168721/
1 2.In the affidavit filed in support of the writ petition, it has been averred by the petitioner that the petitioner is a Partner of the firm M/s.V.N.M.S.Ayyachamy Nadar & Bros., and they imported TOOR WHOLE from TANZANIA and the same has reached the Customs Office.

entities.text: M.Janardhanan vs The Authorized Officer on 29 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondent took sample and sent it to lab for testing.

To his shock and surprise, the petitioner was intimated that the goods which were imported from TANZANIA is not in accordance with the Standard specified under the Food Safety and Standards Act and the Rules, on the reason that the goods have Uric Acid content exceeding the maximum permissible limit and from the referral lab has also the same result;
but according to the petitioner, those two samples were drawn before cleaning and sorting.

Hence,
the petitioner approached the customs office with a request for permission to clean the goods in the presence of the customs officer in view of the circular dated 20th January 2012,
No.1-17/FSSAI/T/2010 and accordingly, now the goods were cleaned based on the said notification.
The petitioner gave a requisition letter to the respondent, but no steps were taken by the respondent to draw the sample for lab testing and the Goods were kept in Wareshouse.
The petitioner has imported the TOOR WHOLE by paying huge money and if the goods are returned to exporter without given opportunity to the petitioner, they will incur heavy loss.
Further, the petitioner undertakes that they will not claim the goods if the result is negative after fresh testing.

Hence, the petitioner has come forward with the present writ petition before this Court for the relief as stated supra.
3.When the matter came up on 02.02.2016, this Court has passed the following interim order_

The respondent is directed to draw joint samples from the consignment under Bill of Entry No.2967947 dated 19.10.2015 and send the same for Lab Testing, keep the results intact, without letting the petitioner know about it.
This order is passed, as an interim measure, to avoid wastage of time, in the event of the petitioner succeeding in the writ petition.

It is made clear that this order will not create any equity in favour of the petitioner, as it is passed only in order to avoid loss of time.
4.Today, when the matter is taken up for consideration, the learned counsel for the respondent submitted that pursuant to the order dated 12.02.2016 passed by this Court, the respondent took samples from the subject consignment of the petitioner and conducted test.

Now, the respondent has filed a report stating that the sample of the subject consignment of the petitioner conforms to the standards laid down under 2.4.6.15 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations 2011
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5.In view of the above report filed by the respondent, the writ petition is allowed, with a direction to the respondent to issue appropriate certificate to the petitioner in respect of the subject consignment.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
No costs.
